title: Only 7% Pass This Midwifery Entrance Exam
summary: Pregnancy, labour, newborn care and calm judgement test what you notice when every detail matters.

landing.intro: Pregnancy, labour and newborn care. Can you stay calm and spot the detail that matters most?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge explores entrance-level midwifery knowledge across 40 varied questions. It covers pregnancy physiology, antenatal wellbeing, labour, newborn care, infection prevention and respectful communication.

The five challenges become progressively more applied, moving from a first appointment into pregnancy and birth foundations, respectful safety, labour and newborn decisions, and a final integrated birth-centre assessment. Questions stay at recognition and judgement level rather than teaching diagnosis or treatment.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers given in this entertainment quiz. It is a playful snapshot of the maternity-care areas that felt strongest and the topics that proved more challenging, not a judgement of clinical competence or suitability for midwifery practice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Work through each maternity-care challenge at your own pace—there is no timer or speed bonus.
Choose the single option best supported by the visible information. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal.
Keep going as the scenarios become harder, then reveal your score and complete answer review.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited midwifery entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Maternity-care procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

checkpoint.finalAdNote: Short ad first — then see your result.

stage-5.preAdCopy: Your result is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Birth Centre Standout
profile-1.copy: You combined strong maternity knowledge with calm, respectful judgement from the first appointment to the final handover. Subtle changes, safety priorities and person-centred choices stayed clear even as the cases became more demanding.

profile-2.title: The Midwifery Natural
profile-2.copy: You showed an excellent feel for pregnancy, birth and newborn-care foundations. Most of the observation, communication and handover traps did not pull you away from the safest supported answer.

profile-3.title: The Calm Candidate
profile-3.copy: You handled a broad mix of maternity knowledge and compassionate decisions with steady reasoning. A few finer details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profile-4.title: The Thoughtful Observer
profile-4.copy: You built a solid result by noticing important clues and treating dignity and safety seriously. Your strongest stage shows where your maternity-care instincts are already taking shape.

profile-5.title: The Promising Applicant
profile-5.copy: You solved a good share of the birth-centre challenge and showed useful instincts across several care areas. The answer review will reveal which foundations are ready for another look.

profile-6.title: The Curious Care Advocate
profile-6.copy: The challenge uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful and respectful judgement. Every answer review offers a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind safe maternity care.

mid-r1q1.question: Which organ supports exchange during pregnancy?

mid-r1q2.question: Why are observations recorded at more than one appointment?
answers: To predict an exact birth time
To notice changes and trends over time

mid-r1q3.question: What does the cervix do during labour?
answers: It gradually opens as labour progresses

mid-r1q4.question: What helps a stable newborn conserve warmth soon after birth?

mid-r1q5.question: When should hands be cleaned around maternity care?
answers: Only at the end of a shift
Before clean contact and after exposure risk

mid-r1q6.question: A woman says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best first response?
answers: Acknowledge the worry and invite her questions
Say there is nothing to worry about

mid-r2q2.question: What is one main role of amniotic fluid?

mid-r2q5.question: A baby’s movement pattern clearly changes from usual. What matters most?
answers: Every baby must move at identical times
Take the change from normal seriously

mid-r2q1.question: Where does a baby normally develop during pregnancy?

mid-r2q3.question: What connects the baby to the placenta?

visual.ariaLabel: Maternal blood to placenta to cord to baby

mid-r2q4.question: Which sequence best represents oxygen reaching the baby?

mid-r3q2.question: A new severe headache appears with visual changes during pregnancy. What is the safest response?
answers: Rest and reassess after an hour
Wait for the next routine appointment
Ask someone at home to keep an eye on the symptoms
Seek prompt assessment from a qualified maternity professional

mid-r3q4.question: A chart records 70, 74 and 78 at three visits. What does it show?

mid-r3q5.question: Which change from an earlier antenatal visit is most important to report clearly?
answers: The appointment was held in a different room
The written note is slightly longer
The visit happened later in the day
The person was well earlier but is now dizzy and noticeably pale

mid-r5q1.question: Which organ provides the muscular contractions of labour?

mid-r5q4.question: The baby is born but the placenta is not yet delivered. Which labour stage is this?

mid-r4q4.question: A woman becomes tearful and says she feels overwhelmed. What should happen first?
answers: Pause, acknowledge how she feels and listen
Reassure her that feeling overwhelmed is common
Try to distract her from what is upsetting her

mid-r5q6.question: Equipment’s sterile wrapper is torn before use. What is the safest response?
answers: Do not treat it as sterile; replace or escalate appropriately
Touch the contents to test them

mid-r4q1.question: A clean procedure is about to begin. What is essential immediately beforehand?
answers: Skip cleaning if hands look clean

mid-r4q2.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the eyes. What is the safest preparation?
answers: Wear ordinary glasses as the only protection
Use appropriate eye or face protection

mid-r4q3.question: A woman says she does not want students present. What is the best response?
answers: Tell her attendance removes that choice
Discuss her refusal in the corridor
Respect her decision and protect her privacy

mid-r4q6.question: A woman asks to consider her options before deciding. What is the respectful response?
answers: Pressure her into the quickest option
Treat questions as refusal of care
Give clear information, answer questions and allow appropriate time

mid-r2q6.question: Before an examination, what should happen first?
answers: Explain it clearly and obtain informed agreement

mid-r7q6.question: Before touching a newborn after handling shared equipment, what is required?
answers: Waiting until the end of the day

items: NOW::Feels feverish · shaking · suddenly much worse
visual.ariaLabel: Earlier comfortable and alert. Now feels feverish, is shaking and suddenly feels much worse.

mid-r6q3.question: Which change matters most?
answers: The time printed on the chart
The fact that labour began earlier
The combined feverish feeling, shaking and marked change from earlier

mid-r7q2.question: Which pattern most strongly suggests a stable newborn may be ready to feed?
answers: Turning towards touch, mouth opening and increasing alertness
Persistent irregular breathing and poor responsiveness
Becoming progressively colder and less active

mid-r7q4.question: What is the basic aim of skin-to-skin contact for a stable newborn?
answers: Support warmth, calm contact and early feeding

mid-r5q2.question: Which visible pattern is most useful when describing contractions?
answers: Their frequency, duration and change over time

mid-r5q3.question: Which change best describes labour becoming more established?
answers: Contractions become generally stronger, longer and more regular
The placenta is always delivered before the baby
The cervix returns to its pre-pregnancy state

mid-r5q5.question: Why can changing position during labour be helpful when safe and comfortable?
answers: It guarantees an exact birth time
It can support comfort and individual coping
It removes the need for observation

mid-r7q1.question: A stable newborn has just been dried but the room is cool. Which approach best supports continued warmth?
answers: Leave the baby uncovered for observation
Use skin-to-skin contact with appropriate warm covering
Separate the baby routinely regardless of circumstances

mid-r7q3.question: A newborn is not feeding as usual and is breathing noticeably faster. What is safest?
answers: Wait several days without telling anyone
Recognise the change and seek prompt qualified assessment

items: PERSON A::Comfortable · alert · routine feeding question
PERSON B::New heavy bleeding · pale · dizzy
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is comfortable and alert with a routine feeding question. Person B has new heavy bleeding and is pale and dizzy.

mid-r10q6.question: Who needs immediate attention?
answers: Person A, because routine questions are quicker
Both can wait for the next handover
Person B, because sudden bleeding, pallor and dizziness show deterioration

mid-r7q5.question: How should a clean, dry umbilical cord stump generally be treated?
answers: Keep it clean and dry and seek advice if concerning changes appear
Pull it to make it detach

mid-r9q1.context: 14:00: comfortable, normal colour, speaking normally. 15:00: breathing faster, pale and increasingly difficult to engage.
mid-r9q1.question: Which change in the handover should receive the greatest attention?
answers: The observation was recorded one hour later
Several new signs show deterioration from the earlier baseline
The first record contains fewer words

mid-r10q1.context: The placenta is the exchange organ. A diagram now shows reduced transfer across it and less oxygen in the cord.
mid-r10q1.question: Which explanation best links both observations?
answers: Reduced placental exchange can mean less oxygen reaches the baby
The stomach supplies the cord directly

mid-r10q2.context: Fluid chart: 650 mL + 450 mL. Observation chart: earlier 74, latest 82.
mid-r10q2.question: What total and trend should be handed over?
answers: 1,100 mL total, with the latest observation higher than the first
1,650 mL total with a falling trend

mid-r10q3.context: Earlier: regular contractions with comfortable pauses. Now: constant severe pain, pallor and faintness.
mid-r10q3.question: What is the safest conclusion?
answers: The regular pattern means every later change is normal
Wait until the next planned check
Choose a named diagnosis before reporting
The sudden multi-clue change needs urgent qualified assessment

mid-r10q4.context: A newborn remains wet and feels cool. Breathing has also become irregular.
mid-r10q4.question: Which response addresses both risks?
answers: Dry the newborn, support skin-to-skin warmth and obtain prompt qualified assessment for the breathing change
Leave wet coverings in place and wait

mid-r10q5.context: The same gloves handled waste and are now reaching towards a clean cord-care pack.
mid-r10q5.question: What should happen before the clean task?
answers: Keep the same gloves because they are intact
Touch the clean pack to test it
Remove contaminated gloves, perform hand hygiene and use appropriate clean equipment
Skip hand hygiene after removing gloves
